202.description: Passphrase update accepted and dispatched; poll the task status for the appliance's result

400.description: Passphrase is not encrypted to the appliance's escrow public key, or the appliance has no registered escrow public key

post.description:
Queue an export of all generated keys encrypted to the caller's public key.

Follow the returned status_url for the job result and its one-time download
handle. Activity is recorded when the artifact is retrieved.

parameters.name: public_key

schema.description: Caller's ASCII-armored OpenPGP public key used to encrypt the exported bundle. Must contain an encryption-capable primary key or subkey.
schema.title: Public Key

405.description: The appliance requires version 10.6 or later and must support this operation

get.description:
Aggregate key counts + backup key + passphrase status; fields beyond the base counts are
gated per-caller by permission (escrow fields also require escrow to be licensed) and omitted
— not nulled — when the caller isn't entitled (DTO ``exclude_if`` fields).

post.description: Request asynchronous escrow for one or more encryption keys.

202.description: Per-key outcomes: a task or a rejection without a task. Failed tasks include customer-safe error details; use task_id to track in-progress tasks.

delete.description: Request asynchronous deletion of an encryption key.

202.description: Request accepted for asynchronous processing to delete the encryption key.

get.description: List key metadata and live task status with permission-scoped fields and cursor pagination.

parameters.name: type

schema.description: Filter by key type. `backup` requires View Backup Keys permission; otherwise returns HTTP 403. Without this permission, omitting the filter returns only volume keys and omits `is_backup_key` from the response.
schema.title: Type

parameters.description: Filter by key type. `backup` requires View Backup Keys permission; otherwise returns HTTP 403. Without this permission, omitting the filter returns only volume keys and omits `is_backup_key` from the response.

parameters.name: is_escrowed

schema.description: Filter by escrow status. Both `true` and `false` require View Key Escrow permission and an enabled Key Escrow license; otherwise returns HTTP 403. If either requirement is missing, omit this filter to list keys with `is_escrowed` excluded from the response.
schema.title: Is Escrowed

parameters.description: Filter by escrow status. Both `true` and `false` require View Key Escrow permission and an enabled Key Escrow license; otherwise returns HTTP 403. If either requirement is missing, omit this filter to list keys with `is_escrowed` excluded from the response.

403.description: The encryption keys feature is unavailable, or View Volume Encryption Keys permission is missing. Also returned when `type=backup` is requested without View Backup Keys permission, or when `is_escrowed=true` or `is_escrowed=false` is requested without View Key Escrow permission or an enabled Key Escrow license.

AiActivateIndexConfigDto.title: AiActivateIndexConfigDto
AiActivateIndexConfigDto.description:
AI Activate search configuration (include/exclude paths) for a volume.

Unified model shared by GET/POST/PATCH request bodies for
``/ai_activate/indexes/{volume_id}``. Fields are optional so PATCH callers
can send only what they want to update; POST callers may omit them to
accept the defaults (empty include/exclude).

``extra="forbid"`` — MCP toggles moved to ``/indexes/{volume_id}/mcp``.
Reject legacy PATCH bodies that include ``mcp_enabled`` here so callers
fail loudly (422) instead of silently having the field ignored.

ApplianceKeysSummaryDto.title: ApplianceKeysSummaryDto
ApplianceKeysSummaryDto.description:
Aggregate key counts + backup key + passphrase status for one appliance (PORTAL-3252).

Every field past ``total``/``generated_count`` is RBAC-gated by permission (and, for escrow
counts, account license): ``exclude_if`` drops the field from the response whenever the
service sets it to the "not entitled" sentinel, the same convention as ``EncryptionKeyDto``'s
``is_escrowed``/``is_backup_key``. ``backup_key`` additionally needs ``null`` (entitled, no
backup key) to stay distinguishable from absent (not entitled), so it defaults to ``UNSET``
rather than ``None``.

a 400. Portal never sees plaintext and forwards it verbatim to the appliance; the
appliance is identified by the path, not the body.

SnapshotStatus.title: SnapshotStatus
SnapshotStatus.description:
Public snapshot lifecycle vocabulary surfaced by the snapshot APIs.

The persisted column (``VolumeEdgeState.current_snapshot_status``)
has a single writer: the EventHub ``VolumeSnapshotStatusProcessor``,
which translates filer ``volume_snapshot_status`` events. No other
code path — API request handlers, heartbeat upserts, background
services — writes to that column. ``cancelling`` never reaches the
DB: it exists as a FE-optimistic wire value only (clients render it
between the cancel dispatch and the filer's ``cancelled`` /
``cancel_rejected`` ack). ``pending`` is a real filer-reported
state.

TaskDto.title: TaskDto
TaskDto.description:
Full/internal task view: the customer summary plus internal steps and
captured auth context.

Produced by the repo/converters and consumed across the backend. It must
not cross the customer boundary as-is — the task routes serialize the
`TaskSummaryDto` subset instead. `auth_context` is the serialized
`AuthContext` (key / user / roles / source_ip) captured at task creation;
event processors re-seed it so audit logs are attributed to the originating
caller rather than the eventhub Lambda identity. Internal-only by design —
never include it on a customer-facing DTO.

TaskFailureDto.title: TaskFailureDto
TaskFailureDto.description:
Customer-safe failure detail for a task: a curated message and when it was
detected.

``message`` is populated only from the task-level curated ``reason`` (the one
customer-safe channel) — never from internal step reasons or raw appliance
text. ``detected_at`` is sourced from the task's ``last_updated_at``. No id:
the enclosing task response identifies the task.

Doctrine: a ``None`` ``message`` means "no curated text"; the backend never
substitutes a generic fallback. Rendering a generic string for the null case is
the frontend's job, so the copy stays localizable.

TaskSummaryDto.title: TaskSummaryDto
TaskSummaryDto.description:
Customer-facing task view: the rolled-up task `state` plus an optional,
curated task-level `reason`.

Deliberately carries no `steps`. Internal step `reason`s — unstructured,
engineering-facing strings (often raw exception detail) — stay in the
backend and never ride on this DTO. The task-level `reason` is a separate,
customer-safe contract persisted when the task becomes failed. It is never
derived from internal step reasons while serving a customer request.

VolumeConnectionItemDto.title: VolumeConnectionItemDto
VolumeConnectionItemDto.description:
One ``(volume, appliance)`` connection row from
``GET /volume_connections``.

The response is denormalised one-row-per-mount (N appliances → N
rows). Nullability mirrors :class:`VolumeApplianceRow` end-to-end —
``None`` means "no data available yet" and is intentionally
distinct from ``0`` / :attr:`SnapshotStatus.idle`.

* ``protocol`` — full deduplicated list in canonical
  SMB → NFS → FTP order; empty if no share configured.
* ``connection_permission`` — derived from
  ``volumes_v2.remoteaccess_autoaccept`` (master) or
  ``volume_edge_states.remoteaccess_permission`` (non-master).
* ``accessible_data`` / ``unprotected_data`` — parsed byte counts;
  ``None`` when the appliance hasn't reported a number.
* ``last_snapshot_utc`` — tz-aware UTC, serialised as ISO 8601.

The trailing per-edge state block (``appliance_hostname`` through
``autofault_folders_count``) carries every column the Volume
Details "Data Protection", "Protocols", "Data Growth", and
"Additional Details" cards need. Kept on this row (rather than a
separate detail endpoint) so ``/volume_connections`` remains the
single low-level resource for per-mount data — Portal's BFF and
external API consumers compose it with ``/volumes/{id}`` to build
higher-level views.

VolumeConnectionsResponseDto.title: VolumeConnectionsResponseDto
VolumeConnectionsResponseDto.description: GET /volume_connections response — all matching mounts (no pagination).

VolumeDetailsDto.title: VolumeDetailsDto
VolumeDetailsDto.description:
Enriched volume response — volume-scoped fields only.

Display fields below are pre-formatted server-side (``protocol``,
``permission_policy``, ``security_mode``, ``snapshot_retention``)
so direct WebAPI consumers see UI-ready values instead of raw filer
enums/bitmasks. The flat ``VolumeDto`` (``GET /volumes/{id}``)
intentionally keeps the raw forms for backward compatibility.

Per-edge state is **not** on this DTO. Callers needing per-mount
data (share/export counts, per-edge schedules, per-edge dirty
bytes, …) call ``GET /volume_connections?volume_id=<id>`` — the
resource split keeps the API resource-oriented and lets external
consumers compose their own views without a UI-shaped
"details+connections" fusion endpoint.

VolumeTelemetrySnapshotDetailsRecord.title: VolumeTelemetrySnapshotDetailsRecord
VolumeTelemetrySnapshotDetailsRecord.description:
Volume snapshot metadata record per appliance.

This provides detailed snapshot information for each appliance, including:
- When the data snapshot phase (P1) started and ended
- When the metadata snapshot phase (P2) started and ended
- Protection metrics and file counts at the time of snapshot

items.description: Snapshot propagation records with statistical analysis
